Subject line: variant_id=BTK-p.Arg28His gene=BTK accession=Q06187 position=28 reference=R alternate=H

Task: PLAN. Objective: given what this mutation breaks, what could a drug act on to correct it? Read the record (hypotheses H1-H3, evidence E1-E19, gaps G1-G6, budget). Propose at least 2 test candidates with expected learning, feasibility and cost, then one plan choosing a single test with a reason for each rejected one. Prefer a test that discriminates H1 from H2. Stay within remaining budget. Then hand off to the orchestrator.

name: record_test_candidate
arguments: {"test_kind": "ligand_contact", "description": "Checks whether residue 28 of BTK sits next to a bound ligand in experimental structures. 39 structures observe residue 28 and hold a non-solvent ligand. A contact with an inositol-phosphate-like or other binding ligand would support H1 (PH-domain ligand binding). No contact across those structures would weaken H1.", "tests_hypotheses": ["H1", "H2"], "expected_learning": 0.7, "expected_learning_reasoning": "H1 is the current favourite and the only one that names a drug-actionable binding surface, so its outcome moves the ranking most. A contact with a ligand would raise H1 above H2 and H3. Absence of any ligand within contact distance across the 39 structures would drop H1 below H2, since H2 would then be the only mechanism left that has evidence (E2, E9, E13). H2 and H3 are not directly scored by this test, so the ranking change is one-sided. The test is also limited: crystal contacts with soluble analogues are not measurements of binding by the variant. G6 says no ligand-residue mapping exists yet, so the outcome is genuinely open.", "feasibility": 0.9, "feasibility_reasoning": "The tool reports can_run true, with 39 experimental structures that observe residue 28 and hold a non-solvent ligand. It uses RCSB PDB neighbour lists, needs no compute seconds and no approval, and costs 2 tool calls. The main risk is data quality, not availability."}
